title: Associated-prime transport from the fibre module to the fibre ring
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime, and put $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, with $j:B\to C$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Let $L$ be any $C$-module, regarded as a $B$-module by restriction of scalars along $j$. Contraction along $j$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Ass}_C(L)\to\operatorname{Ass}_B(L)$. More precisely, for every $z\in L$ the ideal $J=\operatorname{Ann}_C(z)$ contracts to $I=\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)$ and satisfies $J=IC$, and $J$ is prime if and only if $I$ is prime. All primes in $\operatorname{Ass}_B(L)$ contract to $\mathfrak p$ in $A$, so this is the restriction of the fibre prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Residue fields and tensors are [def-weil-residue-field] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; associated primes here mean exact annihilators of elements [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. No flatness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Remark Tag 05E0 (remark-bourbaki), through Lemma Tag 05BY (lemma-ass-quotient-ring) and Lemma Tag 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass), part (1); their argument works for any module over the fibre ring.

proof.text: Write $\varphi:A\to B$ for the given map. By the fraction definition in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], every $\lambda\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ has the form $\overline{a/s}$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p$. Put $u_s=j(\varphi(s))$ and $v_s=1\otimes\overline{1/s}$. The tensor relations give $u_sv_s=1$. Every $c\in C$ is a finite sum $\sum_i b_i\otimes\overline{a_i/s_i}$, by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. With $s=\prod_i s_i$ and $b=\sum_i b_i\varphi(a_i\prod_{h\ne i}s_h)$, bilinearity gives $u_sc=j(b)$, hence $c=v_sj(b)$. The empty sum uses $s=1,b=0$. Thus every element of $C$ has this form with $u_s$ a unit; this proves the fraction description being used, without any assumption on $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass), proof of (1), fraction calculation; Tag 00CO (definition-localization), and Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Fix $z\in L$ and put $I=\{b\in B:bz=0\}$ and $J=\{c\in C:cz=0\}$, the annihilators used in [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Restriction of scalars means $bz=j(b)z$, so $j^{-1}(J)=I$. These sets are ideals by distributivity and associativity of the module action. Since $j(I)\subseteq J$, the ideal $IC$ generated by $j(I)$ is contained in $J$. Conversely, if $c\in J$, express $c=v_sj(b)$ as in Step 1. Then $j(b)z=u_scz=0$, so $b\in I$ and $c=v_sj(b)\in IC$. Hence $J=IC$ for every $z$, including $z=0$.

source.place: Tag 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass), first paragraph of proof; Tag 05BY (lemma-ass-quotient-ring), omitted proof expanded directly

proof.text: If $J$ is prime, its inverse image $I$ is proper because $j(1)=1$, and $bb'\in I$ implies $j(b)j(b')\in J$, so $b\in I$ or $b'\in I$. Thus $I$ is prime. Conversely suppose $I$ is prime. It is proper, so $z\ne0$ and therefore $J$ is proper. If $cd\in J$, choose $c=v_sj(b)$ and $d=v_tj(b')$ by Step 1. Multiplication by $u_su_t$ shows $j(bb')=u_su_tcd\in J$. Step 2 gives $bb'\in I$, so $b\in I$ or $b'\in I$. Multiplication by $v_s$ or $v_t$ then gives $c\in J$ or $d\in J$. This proves that $J$ is prime exactly when $I$ is prime.

source.place: Tag 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass), first paragraph of proof, primality argument written out

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], each associated prime is the exact annihilator of some element. Steps 2 and 3 show that contraction takes $\operatorname{Ass}_C(L)$ into $\operatorname{Ass}_B(L)$, and that for every $I=\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)$ that is prime, $J=\operatorname{Ann}_C(z)$ is a prime with contraction $I$. Thus contraction is surjective on these sets. It is injective because [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] makes contraction injective on all prime ideals of $C$. That same correspondence says that the contraction to $A$ of every such $I$ is $\mathfrak p$. Therefore the obtained bijection is precisely the restriction of the fibre prime correspondence. The argument kept the same element $z$ throughout and used neither flatness nor Noetherianity.
